Japheth
jā'fēth
n. (the third-named son of Noah, father of the northern and western peoples, and the man over whom the enlargement-blessing was spoken)
From Hebrew Yepheth, connected by Noah's own wordplay with pathah, to open wide or make room — hence “God shall enlarge Japheth”. The name is the blessing spoken in it.

Biblical Definition

Japheth is one of the three men through whom the whole present race of mankind descends. Moses is blunt about it: “These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread” (Gen 9:19). After the flood, when Noah lay uncovered in his tent, Japheth and Shem walked backward with a garment upon their shoulders and covered their father without looking on his shame, and the oracle that followed divided the post-flood world into three destinies. Ham's line through Canaan is put under servitude; Shem receives the LORD Himself as his God; and Japheth receives room: “God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem” (Gen 9:27). His sons are named in the first roll of the nations — Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras — and from them the isles of the Gentiles were divided in their lands (Gen 10:5). The northern and western peoples, the maritime and Greek-speaking world that the New Testament will later evangelize, stand in this column. And the enlargement clause is not merely territorial. To dwell in the tents of Shem is to be lodged inside the covenant household of another man's blessing, which is precisely what happens when the Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree and the middle wall of partition comes down.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Japheth; in sacred history he is a son of Noah, brother of Shem and Ham, and the progenitor of the northern and western nations.

expand to see more

JAPHETH, n. A son of Noah, named with Shem and Ham, and the father of seven sons whose families peopled the isles of the Gentiles.

He covered his father with a garment, going backward, and saw not his father's nakedness.

Whence the blessing, God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem.

From his sons Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras are derived the northern and western nations.

The name signifies enlargement, and is expounded in the blessing itself.

Key Scripture

Gen 5:32 — "And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth."

Gen 9:19 — "These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread."

Gen 9:27 — "God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant."

Gen 10:2 — "The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras."

Modern Corruption

The Noahic oracle has been abused for centuries as a charter for racial hierarchy, and is now dismissed as legend by the same handling that once weaponized it. Both readings ignore what the text actually says and to whom.

expand to see more

The oldest abuse of this passage is the reading that turned Noah's words into a permanent ranking of races — Japheth to rule, Shem to worship, Ham to serve. It cannot be got out of the text. The curse falls on Canaan by name, not on Ham and not on any modern people; it was discharged in the conquest of the land under Joshua; and the man on whom it fell has no descendants in any presently identifiable nation. Scripture's own summary of human origins forecloses the whole scheme: God “hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth” (Act 17:26). One blood. Every man in every column of Genesis 10 is a fallen son of Adam needing the same Redeemer, and the mercy that reaches him reaches him on the same terms.

The modern handling makes the opposite error and calls it progress. Because the passage was misused, the passage is discarded — the genealogy relabelled as an ancient ethnic charter with no historical purchase, Noah moved into the category of saga. The dictionary holds Noah historical, the flood worldwide, and the three sons the real fathers of the post-flood race, because the New Testament holds them so and reasons from them. And the honest answer to a text abused is the text read rightly, not the text dropped. Read rightly, Genesis 10 is the most anti-racist chapter in ancient literature: seventy nations, one father, one flood, one promise running toward the day when a multitude no man could number out of every kindred stands before the throne.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yepheth (H3315), Japheth; pathah (H6601), to make wide, enlarge; 'iy (H339), isle, coastland; Greek ethnos (G1484), nation.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yepheth (H3315) — Japheth; the name of Noah's son, tied by the blessing to enlargement.

Hebrew pathah (H6601) — to open wide, make room, enlarge; the verb behind “God shall enlarge”.

Hebrew 'ohel (H168) — tent; to dwell in another's tents is to be received into his household.

Hebrew 'iy (H339) — isle, coast, maritime region; the territory assigned to his sons in Gen 10:5.

Greek ethnos (G1484) — nation, Gentile people; the Septuagint and New Testament word for the peoples of this column.

Usage

"“God shall enlarge Japheth” — a name that is its own prophecy."

"“He shall dwell in the tents of Shem” — room made for the Gentile inside a covenant not first his own."

"“Of them was the whole earth overspread” — three men, one blood, every nation."
